registre-01.why: When you don’t know who the recipient is, the formal address is Madame, Monsieur,. Chère Madame is only for someone you know and excludes a male recipient; Salut à tous is colloquial and never used in a formal letter.

registre-02.why: The fixed expression savoir gré à qqn de faire qqch, in the conditional for politeness: je vous saurais gré de…. serais / aurais are être / avoir and don’t form a set phrase with gré.

registre-03.why: The polite imperative of vouloir is veuillez + inf, the standard form in letter closings. Voulez is indicative and can’t stand alone as an imperative; Veuillent is the third person plural subjunctive.

registre-04.why: nous nous permettons de + inf (we take the liberty of…) is common in formal letters, with the verb agreeing with nous. permettent is the wrong person; permettre is the infinitive and can’t be the main verb.

registre-05.why: The inverted first person singular of pouvoir is puis-je (never peux-je). Puisse-je is subjunctive (a wish form) and can’t form a polite question.

registre-06.why: The polite conditional je voudrais (I would like…). voudrai is the simple future, “I will want to know”, which isn’t a request; veuille is subjunctive and can’t be the verb of a main clause.

registre-07.why: The adjective agrees with salutations (feminine plural) → distinguées. distingués has the wrong gender; distinguée the wrong number.

registre-08.why: prier qqn de faire qqch (to request kindly) is a set phrase in formal letters: nous vous prions de bien vouloir…. prenons / plaisons don’t combine with de bien vouloir.

registre-09.why: être reconnaissant à qqn de faire qqch: the action takes de. à introduces the person thanked; pour only takes a noun, not the infinitive here.

registre-10.why: The fixed closing formula Dans l’attente de votre réponse (with the noun attente). attendant is the present participle (it would be En attendant…); attendu is the past participle and can’t act as a noun after l’.

registre-11.why: Complex inversion with a noun subject: noun + verb-t-pronoun. A verb ending in a vowel needs -t-: propose-t-elle. propose-elle lacks -t-; proposent is the wrong person.

registre-12.why: Complex inversion: La prochaine assemblée aura-t-elle lieu ? A verb ending in a vowel inverted with il/elle takes -t-, with a hyphen on each side. aura-elle lacks -t-; aurat-elle is misspelt.

registre-13.why: craindre que + subjonctif, often with an expletive ne (ne explétif, not negative, part of the written register) → qu’il n’ait. a / aura are indicative.

registre-14.why: je vous prie de + infinitive: in bien vouloir, vouloir stays in the infinitive. veuillez is the imperative and can’t follow de; vouliez is a conjugated form.

registre-15.why: afin de + infinitive (same subject); solliciter is the formal-register “to request”. afin que needs a clause; solliciter is directly transitive and doesn’t take à.

registre-16.why: The task requires a formal register: de nombreuses + noun. plein de and des tas de are colloquial and don’t meet the required written register.

registre-17.why: A formal letter uses emploi (or poste). job is a colloquial English borrowing and taf is slang; neither meets the requirement.

registre-18.why: Written/formal register uses cela; ça is the spoken form of cela; ç’ only appears in speech before être (ç’a été) and is ungrammatical here anyway.

registre-19.why: Polite inverted conditional: Seriez-vous assez aimable pour… ? (Would you be so kind as to…?). Soyez is the imperative and can’t be inverted into a question; Sauriez is savoir and doesn’t go with aimable.

registre-20.why: The fixed business expression accuser réception de qqch (to acknowledge receipt). accuser recevoir / accuser reçu don’t exist (« reçu » only appears in other structures such as un accusé de réception).

registre-21.why: bien vouloir takes an infinitive: bien vouloir examiner. examinez is a conjugated form; examiné is the past participle (pronounced the same and often misspelt in writing).

registre-22.why: The fixed closing formula Je reste à votre disposition (a singular noun, matching votre). dispositions doesn’t match the singular determiner votre; disposé is an adjective/past participle and can’t follow votre.

registre-23.why: The fixed expression en réponse à qqch (in reply to…). en réponse de / pour don’t exist.

registre-24.why: The formal address for someone holding office: Monsieur le Maire / Madame la Ministre (with the definite article). Cher is too familiar; Monsieur Maire lacks the article and isn’t correct usage.

registre-25.why: avant que + subjonctif, in writing often with an expletive ne (not negative). se réunit / se réunira are indicative.

registre-26.why: Inverted question: the je form dois + hyphen + je → dois-je. doit-je is a common misspelling (using the third person form); devrais-tu doesn’t match mon billet (first person) in the sentence.

registre-27.why: être obligé à qqn de faire qqch (to be obliged to someone for doing) → polite conditional nous vous serions obligés. saurions confuses it with savoir gré; aurions obligés is ungrammatical.

registre-28.why: The adjective modifies sentiments (masculine plural) → respectueux. respectueuses / respectueuse wrongly agree with l’assurance (feminine) or Madame.

registre-29.why: se permettre de + infinitive → relancer. relancez is a conjugated form; relancé is the past participle (pronounced like the infinitive, a common written error).

registre-30.why: être reconnaissant(e) de…: the adjective agrees with the writer (je = Mme Leroy, feminine singular) → reconnaissante. reconnaissant is masculine; reconnaissants is plural, wrongly agreeing with vous.
